### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via PageHeaderProps (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55828c5145ce1ca8cb597baf3396614adf9c0583` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2d22ad223808da98ecd82fc66129d212daaa194d` — the merge of head `973897753ed67c2d42a940d934a69d3a41901e17` into base `55828c5145ce1ca8cb597baf3396614adf9c0583`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2d22ad223808da98ecd82fc66129d212daaa194d && git checkout 2d22ad223808da98ecd82fc66129d212daaa194d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 55828c5145ce1ca8cb597baf3396614adf9c0583 973897753ed67c2d42a940d934a69d3a41901e17 && git checkout -B drift-repro 55828c5145ce1ca8cb597baf3396614adf9c0583 && git merge --no-ff 973897753ed67c2d42a940d934a69d3a41901e17

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 55828c5145ce1ca8cb597baf3396614adf9c0583
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 55828c5145ce1ca8cb597baf3396614adf9c0583` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f49c5e9d6539f0281c444f85d3d555cb9a7dabcb`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: PR #23102 body and file list; card #23032 body and its four comments (triage 6124839364, claim 6132299403, dev report 6133354361, seat ACCEPT 6133384711); the net diff `git diff 1badd3183 f49c5e9d6` (4 files, +36 / −3; merge base confirmed as `1badd3183`); the 43 check-runs on the head; objectui at the pinned `.objectui-sha` `7578323a5` (the same pin on `origin/main` and on the head), read with `git show`, no checkout.

Check-runs on the head at read time: 23 success, 8 skipped, 12 in_progress (Build Core, Build Docs, a second Check Changeset run, Test Core 1–6, Type Check consumer gates / debt ledger / workspace), 0 failure. Governed Surface Queue Guard: success. No path in the file list is a governed surface (`.changeset/`, `content/docs/`, `packages/spec/src/`).

### ① Derived judgments

Every clause of the new text was read against objectui at the pin, not against the PR's own account of it.

1. `PageHeaderProps.actions` keeps `z.array(z.string()).optional()`. Accept set: unchanged. RIGHT. The diff moves the `.describe()` string and adds a TSDoc block; nothing else in the schema moves.
2. Describe, clause "resolved against the actions declared on the page's object": `containers.tsx` L1548 `headerObjectName = ctx?.objectName || headerObjectSchema?.name`; L1640 `useMetadataItem('object', headerObjectName)`; L1648 `resolveDeclaredActionIds(authoredHeaderActions, registered)` matches by `name` (`@object-ui/types` `ui-action.ts` L263–282); an unmatched id lands in `unresolved`, is warned once and draws nothing; with no bound object nothing resolves at all. RIGHT.
3. Describe, clause "an authored list is the whole set: an action that declares `record_header` (or `record_more`) in its `locations` but is not named here is not drawn": `headerActionPlan` L1865 `authored = resolvedHeaderActions.filter(placedOnHeader && filterAction)`, and `resolvedHeaderActions` derives from the authored list alone; the only other source merged (L1872) is `hostSystemActions`. No path adds an unnamed object action. RIGHT.
4. Describe, clause "omitting the key draws none of the object's actions": L1582 `rawHeaderActions = schema?.actions ?? schema?.properties?.actions`; undefined gives `authoredHeaderActions = []`, then `resolvedHeaderActions = []`, then `authored = []`; only host chrome survives. Pinned by objectui `page-header-actions.test.tsx` "falls back to the data-page-actions-slot div when no actions provided" (no toolbar) and "renders host system actions even when schema has no actions array". RIGHT as a statement about the node: the synthesizer (`buildDefaultHeader`, `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` L597–607) writes the key onto its own node when it has actions, so a header node that omits the key never draws an object action, whoever produced it.
5. Describe, clause "a named action that declares neither location renders nowhere": `placedOnHeader` L1861 is `actionRendersAt(a, 'record_header') || actionRendersAt(a, 'record_more')`; `actionRendersAt` (`ui-action.ts` L88–101) is `Array.isArray(declared) && declared.includes(location)`, so a missing `locations` and `locations: []` both fail. Spec `action.zod.ts` L996 declares `locations` optional with no default, and L663 / L923 name `locations: []` as the headless declaration, so the case is authorable and reachable. Pinned by "skips an authored action that declares no placement" (undeclared and `[]` alike) and "skips actions whose locations exclude record_header". RIGHT, read in the header's own frame: "nowhere" is neither the inline slot nor the ⋯ overflow, the two locations this header serves; an action placed at `list_item` still draws in a list row, which this key's describe does not speak to.
6. Describe, clause "the host's own Edit / Share / Delete chrome is separate from this list": `RecordDetailView.tsx` L3000–3120 builds `sys_edit` (L3022) / `sys_share` (L3053) / `sys_delete` (L3089) and hands them through `RecordContextProvider headerSystemActions` (L3224); `containers.tsx` L1589 reads them off `ctx.headerSystemActions`, L1872–1874 appends them after the authored actions with no location filter. Pinned by "still renders host system actions that declare no placement". RIGHT as provenance. Precision remark, not a defect: L1875–1883 dedupes by `name` with authored winning, so an object action named `sys_edit` / `sys_share` / `sys_delete` that the list names replaces the host's; objectui documents this as the authored page's opt-out (L1585–1588). The describe says "separate", not "unaffected", and the TSDoc's "whatever it names" speaks of the channel. Borne out.
7. TSDoc bullet "only the platform's synthesized default record page, used when no page is assigned, builds its header from every `record_header` / `record_more` action of the object": `RecordDetailView.tsx` L2740–2748 `recordHeaderActions` is every `objectDef.actions` entry whose `locations` includes `record_header` or `record_more`, deduped by name; L2841 hands it to `synthParts.headerActions`; L3154–3159 `composedPage = assignedPage ? effectivePage : buildDefaultPageSchema(objectDef, { headerActions … })`; `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` L1016–1024 folds them onto the synthesized `page:header.actions` unless a `header` slot overrides. RIGHT. Precision remark: `usePageAssignment.ts` L167–172 maps a `kind: 'slotted'` page to `page: null` plus `slots`, so a slotted assigned page that leaves the `header` slot alone also receives this synthesized header; the qualifier "used when no page is assigned" names the main arm and omits that one. The sentence stays true (it does not say "only when"), and the bullet it qualifies — an authored `page:header` with the key omitted draws none — holds on every arm, a slotted page's own header override included.
8. TSDoc naming `PageHeaderRenderer`, `containers.tsx`, `resolvedHeaderActions` then `headerActionPlan`: all exist under those names at the pin (L1644, L1773), in that order. RIGHT. "A new header action is added to the list as well as to the object" is the whole-list rule's consequence, not a further claim. RIGHT.
9. `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx` sentence "The list is the whole set the header draws: an action that declares `record_header` but is not named is not drawn there, and a header with no `actions` draws none of the object's own actions": items 3 and 4 above; the surrounding paragraph is the Standard Template's authored `page:header`, where the synthesizer is not in play. RIGHT. The pre-existing neighbouring sentence ("`edit` / `delete` / `share` resolve nowhere") is untouched and stays consistent: the host's names are `sys_*`.
10. `content/docs/references/ui/component.mdx` L1525: the table cell is the new describe verbatim (compared against `component.zod.ts` L691). A regenerated row, not a hand edit. RIGHT. `git grep` of the head for the old string "Action IDs to show in header" finds it only in the changeset, which quotes it as the base text; no generated artifact in this repository is left carrying it, so `check:generated` has nothing stale to find. RIGHT.
11. Public surface: the describe ships as the JSON-schema `description` and the generated reference row; the TSDoc ships in the `.d.ts`. Both are text. No export, key, default or enum member moves, and no path under `skills/**` carries the describe. The PR's "no `os lint` rule, no renderer change, no objectui" matches the file list. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/23032-page-header-actions-whole-list.md`: `@objectstack/spec` `patch`. RIGHT. The describe and TSDoc publish from a released package (built JSON schema, `.d.ts`, reference page), so `skip-changeset` would be wrong; nothing is added to the accepted set, so `minor` is not owed. The body's quoted old describe is the base text at merge base `1badd3183`, and "the accepted set of `actions` is unchanged, and no rule or renderer behaviour moves" matches the diff line for line.
- `Clause-②: no`, at line start in the PR body, no arm. RIGHT: the Zod shape is byte-identical, so the accepted set neither widens nor narrows. Not a breaking changeset, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed in the body.
- `Check Changeset` on the head: one run success; a second run in_progress at read time.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (PR acceptance notes, report `deviations` and `out_of_scope_findings`); `open_questions` is empty.

1. "Wording beyond the triage sentence … say if you want them cut back." Answer: keep both. Items 5 and 6 bear them out at the pin, and triage asked for the cheapest remedy that makes the trap visible — a floor on the sentence, not a ceiling.
2. `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md:47` says "ids of the bound object's actions" without saying the list is the whole header; Tier H, outside the dispatched file surface, "carrier: none". Answer: no block on this PR — the dispatch's file surface excluded `skills/**`, and the sentence there is incomplete, not false. Escalated to the seat: that line is the same trap this card names, on the surface an AI author reads first, and "carrier: none" leaves it open; it wants a docs-only Tier H carrier (a card the seat files, or a row in the next governed batch) adding one clause: an authored list is the whole header. This record is read-only and cannot file it.
3. objectui `containers.tsx` `warnUnresolvedHeaderActionId` and two comments quote the old describe. Answer: accepted as noted. A dev-console string in a sibling repo the card excluded; it reads stale after the next pin bump and carries no behaviour. The seat may fold it into the next objectui touch of that file.
4. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally (whole-monorepo build). Answer: accepted; the head's check-runs own it, and the seat reads CI convergence separately — 12 runs were in_progress at read time, none failed.
5. Mid-flight merge of `origin/main` `1badd3183`. Answer: the head's merge base is `1badd3183` and the net diff is exactly the 4 listed files, so the merge introduced nothing.
6. Reviewer's own remarks, both non-blocking and both recorded above: the slotted-page arm the TSDoc's "used when no page is assigned" omits (item 7), and the name-clash dedupe behind "separate from this list" (item 6). Neither sentence is false; either may be sharpened on a later touch of the same text, which is not this card.
